From: chris aubeck <caubeck@yahoo.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2001 21:19:29 +0100 (BST)
Subject: [UFORL] 1661 Tibet - help needed


Dear List Members,

   I have posted the following to colleagues and on
different servers but without much success. Is there
someone on this list who can give me a hand?


    I am trying to trace the original source of an
incident that allegedly occurred in 1661. The story is
as follows:

   Albert d’Orville, a Belgium Jesuit missionary, was
among the first Europeans to travel to Tibet. In a
diary entry dated November 1661, d’Orville remarked on
his own UFO sighting. “My attention was drawn to
something moving in the heavens,” he wrote. “At first,
I thought it might be a species of bird, unknown to
me, that lived in these regions. Then the object came
nearer…”
   What the priest saw was shaped like “a Chinese
double hat” and seemed to rotate as it flew. “The
object winged its way above the city exactly as if it
wished to be admired. It circled twice, and then was
suddenly enshrouded in fog, and as much as I strained
my eyes I could no longer see it.”
   D’Orville asked a nearby lama whether he, too, had
seen the object, or whether it had been an
hallucination. The lama’s reply probably left the
Jesuit as astonished as it left me when I first read
Hartwig Hausdorf’s book, The Chinese Roswell, where
d’Orville’s account is reproduced in full:

‘My son, what you witnessed just now was not magic,
because beings from other worlds travel across the
oceans of space, and it was they who breathed the
spirit into the first people who lived on this earth.
These beings condemn all violence; they counsel
mankind to love one another. Their teachings are like
seeds, but if these seeds are sown on rocky ground,
they cannot germinate. These beings, who are
light-skinned, are always received by us in
friendship, and they often come to earth near our
monasteries. They have continued to instruct us,
revealing truths that were lost in the centuries of
cataclysm which have changed the face of the earth.’
The facts:

i) I know for certain that Albert d’Orville did exist
and wrote about his explorations of Tibet in the 1660s
(accompanied by fellow Jesuit Johann Grueber of
Austria, d’Orville travelled on foot from China
through eastern Tibet to Lhasa, and then to India,
between 1661 and 1664).

ii) The English text reproduced above is from Hartwig
Hausdorf’s “The Chinese Roswell” (1994, p.88-89).

iii) Hausdorf took the reference from Der
Gotter-Schock (Munich, 1992), a book written by Swiss
researcher Erich von Däniken. I have not seen this
book, so I don’t know what von Däniken’s source was.

iv) However, a stroke of luck brought me to an
excellent Spanish case-book, “Fenómeno OVNI” Volume
II, published by Inapp, Madrid 1979. On page 391 an
article entitled “Maestros de Otros Mundos en el
Tibet” provides the same alleged diary entry, in
Spanish. It quotes an Italian publication.

v) The source quoted is the book “Los Extraterrestres
Existen” by Gianni Lucarini. This book is unknown to
me.

vi) According to the Spanish article, Lucarini’s
source was the Italian publication “La aviación de
otros planetas.”

Can anyone tell me any more?

Chris Aubeck

Subject: [UFORL] Ministry of Defence's 'Rendlesham' File

Now online, Ian Ridpath's related comments and a significant,
April 2001, interview with Nick Pope, answering question from
Dave Clarke and Andy Roberts:

http://www.flyingsaucery.com/rendlesham/comment.htm

The interview with Pope confirms my contention that he was never
aware the Ministry of Defence did in fact hold a 'Rendlesham'
file, which documented their reaction to Halt's memo.

A notable extract in light of recent developments:

Clarke: I don't want to prattle on about Rendlesham for too long,
and there are other important cases, but I want to ask you do you
think there is anything else to emerge?

Pope: Not from the official records in Britain, no.
[END]


As he was so evidently oblivious to the existence of this 'Holy
Grail' of Britains' 'UFO' documentation, first obtained by Dr
Clarke from the Ministry in May this year, perhaps the UK's self-
styled 'Fox Mulder' can explain why Georgina Bruni claims Pope
had duly studied that 'X-File':

"Nick Pope worked on the entire file (and numerous others) for
three years and has confirmed to me that in many respects Randles
and Easton (and indeed Clarke and others associated with this
report) have simply misunderstood the way in which the military
and government work. On this I have to agree".

Some might conclude it was Pope who clearly had no idea how the
Government worked.

Given that the UK still doesn't have an equivalent to America's
'Freedom of Information Act', the acquisition of this paramount
material - an extraordinary insight into official investigations
concerning one of the most significant 'UFO' cases of all time -
is an exceptional achievement.

As the contents merely substantiate the absurdity of any 'UFO
cover up' claims, perhaps when fully absorbed, this will be
recognised as a landmark research breakthrough, albeit hugely
disappointing to 'UFO cover up' aficionados world-wide.

Subject: [UFORL] Sir Fred Hoyle

Fred Hoyle died this past week. NY Times and BBC obituary links are
posted below.

http://www.nytimes.com/2001/08/22/obituaries/22HOYL.html?ex=999144000&en=0
e0c6a4565011062&ei=5040&partner=MOREOVER

http://news.bbc.co.uk/hi/english/uk/newsid_1503000/1503721.stm

Hoyle was one of the main proponents of the Panspermia Theory for the
origin of life on Earth, a theory which is gaining more and more
attention among the scientific community.

It was his role and published writings in the 1950s on the cosmological
origin debates against over whether the Big Bang (a term he created) or
the Steady State theories (a theory he then championed more on
philosophical grounds than scientific) that got me wondering about a
populated universe and the possibility of extraterrestrial life emerging
throughout the universe and indirectly interested in UFOs.

For those interested in Sir Fred Hoyle and the Panspermia Theory, one
can go to the What's New link on:

http://www.panspermia.org/

From: "James Easton" <voyager@ufoworld.co.uk>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2001 17:48:20 +0100
Subject: Re: [UFORL] Ministry of Defence's 'Rendlesham' File

I've obtained what is understood to be a press release, issued by
Georgina Bruni. I believe she is scheduled to appear on the
regional news program 'Look East' later tonight.

Amongst the claims made in an attempt to scrape together any
'evidence' which implies the MoD's files reveal a 'UFO cover up'
- despite the abject reverse being so comprehensively documented
therein - are some continued assertions from Nick Pope.

As recently highlighted in the latest 'Voyager' newsletter and
also on this list, Pope originally went into great detail
explaining during various interviews how there was no MoD
'Rendlesham file', because the Ministry didn't even bother
investigating Halt's memo. So far as he was aware anyway.

Now, Bruni informs the media that she obtained a different story
direct from Pope himself:

"In fact the MOD files reveal that Nick Pope took enough of an
interest in the Rendlesham case to began further enquiries,
whilst at the same time being forced to comply with MOD policy by
doing what his predecessors did, spinning the usual MOD line. But
there is no doubt that he was considered by ufologists to be the
most active and helpful person to have ever sat at the UFO desk.
I thought it would be interesting to ask him for his opinion on
the release of these files. He told me........

'I recognise most of the documents from my time in Secretariat
(Air Staff)'."


How can Pope recognise most of the 155 documents when he claimed
- after having left 'Secretariat(Air Staff)2a':

"The standard line on Rendlesham Forest is that the incident was
looked into, and nothing of defence significance was uncovered.
The challenge, as it where, to the department, is that we have
never seen the analysis".

As he also confirmed, when interviewed by Dave Clarke and Andy
Roberts in April this year - just before the MoD file was
released to Dr Clarke:

"I find Rendlesham bizarre; looking at the Rendlesham Forest
file, it starts obviously with Halt's memo and Don Moreland's
covering note and then frankly there isn't a lot. In fact, as
I recall, I don't think there is anything until the News of the
World and Chuck de Caro's documentary, some papers from the
Public Affairs Office 3rd Air Force about the handling of
this and then it turns into correspondence".

Asked - there must be something missing there then? - Pope
replied:

"Something missing or missing a trick, but it depends what you
mean. If you look very carefully at what you have been told about
Rendlesham, it says I think nothing more than Colonel Halt's
report was examined carefully at the time by those officers
responsible for looking at the Air Defence of the realm and the
conclusion was that nothing of any defence significance was
involved and as such no further action was taken. Well, that is
I'm sure technically a true statement. Whether it implies that
anyone actually sat down and did any sort of sucking of teeth,
you know, interviewing of witnesses, etc I don't think it does -
I think if that memo arrived to DS8 at the time, side-copied to
two or three specialist divisions and if it had sat on file with
nothing else being done then the statements made on Rendlesham
are still true; it was examined by, because when it came out of
the envelope it would have been read, so it was examined by, and
its almost chicken and egg by virtue of the fact that they placed
it on the file and didn't do any investigation with a capital I,
you could say well, its an assumption of course...".


Clearly, if Pope had in truth ever seen the papers now released
he wouldn't have to make "an assumption" that the Ministry's
entire case 'examination' comprised someone having a cursory read
of Halt's memo before sticking it in a file!


Perhaps he will explain the apparently incongruous divergence
[which I understand local media sources are now aware of] in his
claimed recollections.


James Easton.

Subject: [UFORL] Media Broadcast Alert

Slightly off-topic, although with a parallel to proclaimed
'cover-ups' and what's subsequently revealed by official 'secret'
documents - on UK radio tonight:

Radio 4 @ 8:00 p.m.

DOCUMENT:
The investigative series in which a document is used to shed new
light on the past...

'The Day They Made It Rain'
Presented by Mike Thomson

On 15 August 1952, the village of Lynmouth in Devon witnessed a
devastating flood which cost 34 lives. The rain was so hard it
didn't seem entirely natural; some said it wasn't. Thomson looks
at new evidence on the imprecise science of cloud seeding,
revealing who had secrets to keep....

This programme finds evidence that there were secret cloud
seeding experiments over southern England in the days before the
flood.
[END]


I'm sure this will be of general and/or 'fortean' interest to
some subscribers and Radio 4 broadcast's are available over the
Internet - see:

http://www.bbc.co.uk/radio4/index.shtml


As it happens, there are a couple of other topical programs which
might be worth staying on for:

9:00 Science and Magic

In the second of two programmes recorded at the Royal Society,
Trevor Phillips discusses the future of scientific method with Dr
Joan Leach, Dr Marcus du Sautoy, Dr Serena Roney-Dougal and
Professor Bernard Carr. Newtonian science's emphasis on
measurement, experiment and proof seems increasingly ill-equipped
to answer questions about the cosmos or parapsychology. Have we
reached the point where a new system of investigation is needed,
one that allows subjectivity, in the form of consciousness, into
the scientific framework? Are scientists set to become alchemists
once more?


9:30 Devout Sceptics

Bel Mooney and her guest explore the territory between belief and
unbelief.

Rob,

Yes, he would still be required to comply with the Official
Secrets Act, even if no longer a government employee.

If Pope _had_ been aware of the file contents now released, there
might have been some issues about what could be revealed.

However, it seems clear he had no idea most of these documents
existed and believed the Ministry of Defence never investigated
Halt's memo.

As we can see above, Pope did in fact describe what was in the
file he was familiar with.


The following is from an Interview Pope gave to UFO Magazine on 5
May, 1996, when he spoke about the 'Rendlesham' case::

UFO: Would it not have been different given such an incident had
occurred whilst you headed Sec(AS)2a? Would you have launched an
investigation?

Nick Pope: I would have been on the first bloody train to
Bentwaters!

UFO: What kind of support would you have given?

Nick Pope: I would have taken soil samples, and taken those to
the Defence Radiological Protection Service. I would have
immediately impounded the radar tapes and had them sent to me,
and immediately called RAF defence experts in, we would have sat
down, looked at the tapes and analysed the content to see if they
showed structured craft or spurious returns. Interview statements
would have followed...

UFO: But this allegedly did not happen in 1980?

Nick Pope: At the end of the day this did not happen, so far as I
am aware.
[END]


Pope was evidently unaware that the Ministry did make related
enquiries.

Indeed, he was then directly asked, "Perhaps DS8 did these things
and there was a general clamp down of information?" and replied,
"If that had been the case it would have inevitably leaked out".
It's only officially 'leaked out' now and one must surmise why
Pope reportedly claims he recognises "most" of the released
documents and the investigations they confirm.

Perhaps it's considered an embarrassment that in all his comments
about a case which Pope termed "the Holy Grail of Ufology', he
was oblivious to the critical facts known to others within his
own department.

He is, after all, the 'real Fox Mulder'.

Allegedly.


Why not simply admit, as the evidence obviously indicates, how
during his three year tenure, when he was chiefly responsible for
non-operational RAF activities overseas and obtaining diplomatic
clearance policy for military flights abroad - with, according to
the Ministry, "a small percentage of time dealing with the public
about alleged 'UFO' sightings" - that he was clueless about what
action the Ministry did in fact undertake concerning
'Rendlesham'.

This is a topic - entertaining, if not also perhaps in some
instances intriguing - which was discussed on UFORL's
predecessor, 'UFO Skeptics'.

The most prolific source of online material seems to be Matthew
Hurley's updated web site [some new images I haven't seen
published anywhere else], at:

http://homepage.ntlworld.com/m.hurley/


There's one significantly documented 'UFO' I noticed which, if we
hadn't known otherwise, would surely be cited as paramount
evidence of a possible alien spacecraft [and those witnessing it]
- 'Halley's Comet' as depicted in the Bayeux tapestry - see:

http://www.getty.edu/artsednet/resources/Space/Stories/halleys.ht
ml

[this URL will 'wrap around']


Given how the Bayeux 'documentation' must have been based on
observations where the story was eventually very much 'second
hand', is it that far removed from 'Halley's Comet' as it would
have been perceived?

Could similar historical artwork, particularly the often cited
fresco from the altar at 'Visoki Decani Monastery' in Kosovo,
possibly have been of a comet or meteor?

Assuming of course that the Bayeux tapestry does show a
representation of 'Halley's Comet' and not, coincidentally,
'something else from outer space...'.

From: "Robinson, Larry" <lrobins@indiana.edu>
Date: Tue, 4 Sep 2001 17:58:06 -0500
Subject: RE: [UFORL] 'UFOs' in Historical Artwork



---- -X =@ o_= X<= <o> o-< <-I-= -> <O-O-O< <-88 ----
Larry Robinson S/AP/EIS     lrobins@indiana.edu
Indiana University      (812) 855-5073 Room 42
Kinesiology Dept        http://php.indiana.edu/~lrobins
1025 E 7th St     Rm 112 HDTV and taxes killed RCA.
Bloomington IN 47405-7109

Some of those "UFOS" were depictions of common things by
artists who had their own ideas about them.

In the 14th century tapestries and other works, those hat shaped
things are just stylized clouds. They are common in a lot of works
from that time.

In the 1338 painting, the big ball is just the artist's idea of the sun.

In the 1350 painting, those objects are the sun and moon, with the
pagan gods they were believed to be.

In "Le Tebaide", that's a real shield on the ground. The perspective
is horrible because perspective had not become a true art until later.

In "The Annunciation with Saint Emidius" and "The Madonna with
Saint Giovannio", those are artist's depictions of the Holy Spirit.

In "Theatrum Orbis", this is a known, but rare solar halo phenomenon.

In the 1710 "The Baptism of Christ", the artist attempted to depict
the heavens opened, as related in Matthew 3:16; Mark 1:10; and
Luke 3:21-22.

From: "James Easton" <voyager@ufoworld.co.uk>
Date: Wed, 5 Sep 2001 04:03:49 +0100
Subject: Re: [UFORL] Beyond The Truth (Nick Pope)...

Regarding:

>From: <dominicbunnell@mail.com>
>To: <UFORL@yahoogroups.com>
>Subject: [UFORL] Beyond The Truth (Nick Pope)...
>Date: 04 September 2001 23:50

Dominic wrote:

>There is a programme on ITV1 tonight at 23:30 in the u.k. It
>looks into the work of Nick Pope during his time at the Ministry
>Of Defence UFO desk. It is a repeat so most of you have probably
>seen it before but I thought i'd just mention it anyway.
>
>Beyond The Truth
>ITV1

Dominic,

I don't recall seeing this program before and unfortunately, it
wasn't shown by my local ITV region.

The title is however aptly topical and I see that in his latest
newsletter, Pope now claims, concerning the recently released
Ministry of Defence [MoD] 'Rendlesham' documents:

"The documents come from a file (or more accurately, from several
different files) that I used during my tour of duty in Sec(AS)2a,
from 1991 to 1994".

As so many others appreciate, the factual anomaly which
strikingly asks to be resolved is whether any MoD file Pope
actually had access to contained, as he seems to insinuate, those
documents which have been made available.

Pope, for some reason, doesn't say this.

Straightforward questions for Nick Pope:

1. Long before the MoD file was made public, you claimed in an
inaugural, May 1996, 'UFO Magazine' interview that, so far as you
were aware:

"The standard line on Rendlesham Forest is that the incident was
looked into, and nothing of defence significance was uncovered.
The challenge, as it where, to the department, is that we have
never seen the analysis ".

If you had never 'seen the analysis', then why are you,
seemingly, asserting being familiar with the documents Dr Clarke
has published?


2. You told 'UFO Magazine', that, had you been involved at the
time of 'Rendlesham', then "radar tapes" would have been
impounded and "RAF defence experts called in". These were in fact
actions instigated by the MoD.

Yet, when asked by 'UFO Magazine', "But this allegedly did not
happen in 1980?... you replied, "At the end of the day this did
not happen, so far as I am aware".

They further queried, "Perhaps DS8 did these things and there was
a general clamp down of information?".

You denied any knowledge; "If that had been the case it would
have inevitably leaked out".

How does this equate with your present recollections of the
MoD/'UFO' facts?


3. When more recently interviewed by Dave Clarke and Andy
Roberts, again prior to the MoD file's 'absolute zero cover-up
revelations', you acknowledged:

"I find Rendlesham bizarre; looking at the Rendlesham Forest
file, it starts obviously with Halt's memo and Don Moreland's
covering note and then frankly there isn't a lot. In fact, as I
recall, I don't think there is anything until the News of the
World and Chuck de Caro's documentary, some papers from the
Public Affairs Office 3rd Air Force about the handling of this
and then it turns into correspondence".

As Dave and Andy surmise:

"It is apparent that Pope did not have access to the documents
relating to the investigations made in 1981-83 by DS8 and RAF
(Ops) that were released by the MOD in 2001. These did not, in
1992-4, form part of the "correspondence file" on the Rendlesham
case that Pope accessed whilst serving at Sec (AS) 2. Why Pope
did not have access to the newly-released material is a mystery.
Did he not feel it necessary to request a search for additional
documents, or did he not have sufficient 'need to know' to see
them? If the former was the case, it hardly supports his
contention that it was this incident in particular that helped to
persuade him of the existence of ET visits to Britain".

Given that it's comprehensively documented you had no knowledge
of the Ministry's research, is the true scenario as 'potentially
suggested' in a recent 'UFO Research List' commentary:

"Perhaps it's considered an embarrassment that in all his
comments about a case which Pope termed "the Holy Grail of
Ufology', he was oblivious to the critical facts known to others
within his own department.
[END]


I also understand that Graham Birdsall of 'UFO Magazine' now
states on their web site:

"In revealing how officials briefed Ministers to deliberately
mislead both houses of Parliament, what emerges from these files
is a 20-year-long official cover-up that stretches to the highest
echelons of government".

Why does Graham seemingly ignore the contrary fact that Pope told
'UFO Magazine' in 1996:

UFO Magazine: Was there a cover-up?

Nick Pope: No. Not in the MoD - I think the MoD's response was
just ineffective.

UFO: That's a very big statement?

Nick Pope: Yes, but if something of that magnitude was reported
and simply placed on file, then what else can you say?


It's a confirmation Pope repeated, for example, in a later 1996
interview with CNI News:

CNI News: This seemingly irrational denial of significant UFO
events could be interpreted as evidence of a deliberate cover-up.
What are your views on that?

NP: I found no evidence to support a cover-up in Britain. I
think, without trying to sound too arrogant, that I would have
gotten a few hints in three years if there had been someone doing
my job but on a covert basis...".


A stupendous irony is Pope's response when, some years ago, asked
that same question by a certain Georgina Bruni:
Bruni: Do you think there's a cover-up in the UK?

Pope: I don't think it's so much a case of a cover-up, I think
it's just that there's no lasting evidence and I don't think the
officialdom know how to deal with it. I think that officialdom is
just not convinced that there's any real proof.


Doubtless these fundamental discrepancies will be prominently
debated by Birdsall, Bruni and Pope at the imminent 'UFO
Magazine' conference, where they are all presenters of the
same... err.. different... 'evidence'.

Then again, who knows... maybe the contradictions won't even be
mentioned at all. Will Pope accede to a celebration of
allegations which he has so comprehensively refuted and say
nothing in 'defence'...?

At present, we can only highlight on UFORL these seemingly
incongruous 'UK UFO cover-up' verdicts and inherent, elementary
questions.


James Easton.

Subject: RE: [UFORL] 'UFOs' in Historical Artwork

I've just checked the depiction of 'Halley's comet' in the Bayeux Tapestry.

The Latin above the people pointing at it (ISTI MIRANT STELLA) means "they
admire the star". It's common in medieval Latin text to find that all comets
are attributed to a single wandering star.

So nothing mysterious there, then...

Friday September 7 12:15 PM ET

US Has Heavily Researched Anti-Gravity, Book Says

By Bradley Perrett

LONDON (Reuters) - The U.S. military may have conducted serious
research into anti-gravity based on Nazi studies, a top defense
journalist suggests in a new book.

In ``The Hunt for Zero Point,'' journalist Nick Cook says, based
on a decade's research, he believes by the 1950s the U.S. was
seriously working on anti-gravity ``electrogravitics''
technology, which would lift and propel vehicles without wings or
thrust.

``I feel intuitively that some vehicle has been developed,
particularly given that there is this wealth of scientific data
out there, and the Americans have never been slow to pick up on
this sort of science,'' Cook, the aerospace consultant for Jane's
Defense Weekly, told Reuters in an interview.

Cook uncovered reports and sightings of a Nazi research device
that had been hidden in a remote part of Poland, where it had
apparently been supplied with great quantities of electricity --
which an electrogravitic experiment would require.

Curiously, barely a hint of such Nazi research appeared after the
war, suggesting that whoever captured it -- probably the United
States -- immediately stamped it ``secret,'' he said.

Cook noted that, as a respected expert, he is risking his
reputation by writing seriously about a technology associated
with UFOs, which most scientists dismiss as science fiction
embraced by ``hocus-pocus'' believers.
The United States is known to have a huge budget for so called
``black projects,'' because it spends more on defense than can be
accounted for by adding up the value of public programs.

Cook admitted he cannot produce a conclusive case. But that is
the nature of black projects, in which even the workers usually
have no idea what they are working on.

In 1947, amid the early craze of UFO reports, an air force
general reported on the possibility of the United States building
disc-shaped objects with extreme rates of climb and
maneuverability but without noise or evident propulsion.

In the mid 1950s electrogravitics was the subject of a few press
reports, including one that described work by most of the United
States' major defense contractors, Cook reported.

And then it all went quiet -- just as stealth technology suddenly
disappeared from view in the mid 1970s, only to re-emerge as
operational aircraft in the late 1980s.

Academic papers on the subject have mysteriously disappeared from
libraries.

There is still no firm evidence that electrogravitics is more
than science fiction. Civilian scientists and amateurs have
experimented with it, and while some have reported success, no
one seems to have reproduced their results to prove that it
works.

Subject: Nazi UFOs And All That


Dear All,

Nice to be back.

Jane's Defence Weekly's very own Aerospace expert Nick Cook has
just had his 'The Hunt For Zero Point' published by Century in
the UK. Several people have e-mailed me to congratulate me on
having published the bulk of material in 'UFO Revelation' over
two years ago. In fact, Cook didn't use many of the documents
that I did, but he concentrated much more on "anti-gravity"
technologies. Nevertheless, Cook has made some very important
new discoveries and, with Bill Rose's continued efforts and
those of Canadian Aerospace historian Bill Zuk, we now have an
emerging and improved picture of Nazi and man-made flying disc
technologies.

Hand in hand with Cook's new revelations and proof that Avro
Special Projects Groups leader John CM Frost travelled, in 1953,
to a highly secret meeting in Germany with a senior scientist
(probably Richard Miethe) to discuss German flying disc
technologies of the wartime period, the skeptics will no doubt
be wheeling out the usual emotional stuff about concentration
camps and so forth to divert attention away from the
technological/aviation side. However, like so much of our
evidence, this material comes straight from the Canadian defence
archives.
As our group has said before, this is a technical investigation.
Whilst I have always concentrated upon Counter Intelligence
Corps, CIA and other declassified documents to make forward
progress, colleagues have combed other areas for new evidence.
Despite the skeptic's claim (Kevin McClure, for instance) that
"no new evidence" could emerge over 50 years after the end of
hostilities, new evidence continues to come out!

The latest development is a group photograph showing Richard
Miethe with known Paperclip scientists taken in Germany in 1945.

Nick Cook deliberately has, very understandably, steered away
from the 'UFO' aspects of his investigation although the links
are pretty clear. It's just nice to have one of the world's
leading experts in aerospace and black technologies reopening an
important debate with the timely publication of an undoubted
bestseller.

With this in mind, I shall be "spilling the beans" on many of
the latest developments and recapping the solid evidence for
man-made advanced flying discplanes on the Jeff Rense radio show
in a the very near future.

In the meantime, the game's afoot.


Tim Matthews

Author, UFO Revelation
British UFO Studies Centre

<BR>
<BR>"Sikorsky CYPHER II UAV Conducts First Flight"
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>STRATFORD, Conn., July 5, 2001 - The Sikorsky CYPHER II Unmanned Air
Vehicle
<BR>(UAV) reached a major milestone here on June 15 with its first tethered
<BR>flight. This marked the first time the experimental aircraft has taken to the
<BR>air. CYPHER II has since maintained a rigorous, almost daily test flight
<BR>schedule.
<BR>
<BR>The aircraft is being built for the U.S. Army Night Vision Labs in Fort
<BR>Belvoir, Va., and will be used for testing small sensors next year. "Sikorsky
<BR>has performed admirably to achieve first tethered flight on the CYPHER II
UAV
<BR>despite the significant technical challenges typically faced with
<BR>developmental aircraft," said Gary F. Meyering, Small Unmanned Air Vehicle
<BR>Project Leader at the Night Vision Labâ€™s Air Systems Division. "This was a
<BR>considerable milestone and we would like to thank the entire CYPHER II team
<BR>for its selfless hard work and dedication."
<BR>
<BR>Tethered flight allows the CYPHER II team to limit the flight envelope of the
<BR>unmanned vehicle. The next milestone will be a free flight scheduled by the
<BR>end of summer at Sikorsky's Development Flight Center in West Palm Beach,
<BR>Fla.
<BR>
<BR>"The Army looks forward to the capabilities this unique new platform will
<BR>bring to Future Combat System (FCS) development, where Vertical Take-off
and
<BR>Landing air vehicles will provide the ground commander with an organic
<BR>Reconnaissance Surveillance and Target Acquisition capability and improved
<BR>situational awareness," Meyering said.
<BR>
<BR>The CYPHER II incorporates shrouded rotor technology developed on the
CYPHER
<BR>Technology Demonstrator (TD) aircraft. The addition of wings and a pusher
<BR>propeller provides high speed capability. The shrouded rotor is safer than
<BR>exposed rotor systems typically used on rotary-wing UAVs because it
minimizes
<BR>the hazard of exposed high speed rotor blades to ground personnel. The
<BR>aircraft has a 10-foot wing span, weighs about 250 pounds at mission weight
<BR>and is capable of 135 mile per hour forward flight speed.
<BR>
<BR>The CYPHER II with its unique removable wing design can hover like a
<BR>helicopter or be flown as a fixed wing aircraft. The air vehicle incorporates
<BR>cutting-edge technology that makes it ideally suited for urban surveillance,
<BR>communications relay, precise payload delivery, and operations in crowded
<BR>terrain.
<BR>
<BR>As a fixed wing aircraft, the CYPHER II UAV has a maximum range of more
than
<BR>100 nautical miles. As a rotary wing aircraft, the CYPHER II UAV can operate
<BR>in confined areas and support urban operations.
<BR>
<BR>Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation, based in Stratford, Conn., is a world leader
<BR>in helicopter design, manufacturing and service. Sikorsky is a subsidiary of
<BR>United Technologies Corporation (NYSE:UTX), of Hartford, Conn., which
<BR>provides a broad range of high-technology products and support services to
<BR>the aerospace and building systems industries.
<BR>
<BR>For more information, contact Bill Tuttle at (203)386-3829 or Ed Steadham at
<BR>(203)386-6086.
<BR>

From: YoungBob2@aol.com

Subject: Re: [UFORL] Beyond Belief

James, List:

It is, indeed, beyond belief. Like one of the rediculous action
movies. I can't help feel that tomorrow morning I will wake up
and all of this will be a bad dream.

I am an amateur astronomer and have noticed something tonight
that I haven't seen in my memory. NO air traffic. Nothing. There
are almost always 3 or 4 planes, often small, with their flashing
anti-collision lites. And no trains for hours on the bridge next to
my house, it's usually quite busy. It is truly surreal in a dark, quiet
sky with sparkling stars.

I'm located in Harrisburg, roughly half way between New York
and Washington and a little to the West. We're going to the
hospital first thing in the morning to give blood, they're calling for
donors. Our town is sending fire fighters tomorrow to relieve
those in NY and surrounding places.

I remember Three Mile Island, which is about 8 miles from here.
And my parents often told me about the day they learned of Pearl
Harbor, which for us was the beginning of WWII. I guess this
must be what it was like.

I just heard that the losses in the Pentagon building, alone, are
over 800 dead. Of the first 11 fire companies to reach the world
trade buildings, half were lost, over 200, some trying to carry out
weelchair-bound people. I'm afraid the news over the next days
is going to be terrible.

And to be perfectly honest with you, what I'm hearing from almost
everyone is anger, real deep anger. God help us.

This surreal quiet in a beautiful starry night sky, and sadness and
anger. That's about it, tonight.

Clear skies, tomorrow, my friends:

Bob Young

I have a friend who lives near New York and who I realised might
have been part of the emergency services units involved.

although he had been on duty, it wasn't near the devastation.

the scene was like not long after the towers had collapsed.

I only reveal this because it is a documented snapshot of that
abject reality and one which, when fully taken in, maybe helps to
further begin setting those appalling events in perspective:

"I don't know if the free world will ever be the same after this,
this attack will have far more devastating consequences other
than the destruction of property and loss of life. The dead will
probably number in the tens of thousands.

Some people I know who have deployed down there to assist, have
called back and said there are so many body parts in the area of
destruction that they just drive over them to try and get to the
living that are trapped in the rubble".


This vision of hell from yesterday, and how only seven(?) from
thousands 'walked out alive' today, is surely a mere glimpse of
the shocking horror what is yet to unfold.

We can perhaps expect as a result that many related issues will
become redefined in a new perspective, especially seething anger
and what constitutes an 'appropriate military response'.

From: "Greg Sandow" <greg@gregsandow.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Sep 2001 22:57:15 -0400
Subject: RE: [UFORL] Beyond Belief

> This vision of hell from yesterday, and how only seven(?) from
> thousands 'walked out alive' today, is surely a mere
> glimpse of
> the shocking horror what is yet to unfold.

The horror is, as the subject of this thread indicates, almost
beyond belief. Three New York newspapers ran photos this morning
of people jumping to their deaths, their bodies looking almost
peaceful as they fell through the air. The New York Daily News
featured a photo of a severed hand, found on the street in the
disaster area. One firefighter spoke on TV about watching his
partner die when a body from a high floor in one of the towers
fell on him. Right now there's a poisonous stench in New York,
extending uptown at least to 47th Street, where Anne and I live,
from the site of the calamity.

But I want -- with a great sense of relief -- to correct any
notion that only seven people of the thousands who worked in the
World Trade Center survived this. I'm not sure if that's what
James is saying, but things are far better than that. Many people
escaped or were evacuated from the buildings in the more than an
hour that passed between the time the planes hit, and the
collapse of the towers. It's possible that these were the
majority of the people who worked there.

The low number given here and elsewhere for survivors is the
number of people found alive in the rubble in the day and a half
since the collapse. That was nine, last I heard. Apparently
others are still alive. They can be heard crying out from the
rubble, and some have made cell phone calls. But the number of
people who survived the event, by getting out before the
buildings collapsed, is much higher.

One aspect of the horror takes a while to sink in. Surely, though
a great many people survived, thousands are dead. But it seems as
if nobody knows at this point who many of them are. Families
haven't been contacted; no list of the dead has, as far as I
know, been even privately assembled. All anyone knows right now
is that many, many people are missing. So local TV in New York
has been full of heartrending scenes from New York hospitals.
People go there with the desperate hope of locating missing
friends and family. Tearfully, or in shock, they get a minute or
so on TV, to hold up pictures of their missing loved ones, and to
give a phone number where they can be reached, if someone has
some information.
I wonder, watching all this, if many of the dead will ever be
found and identified. Maybe we'll only develop the true death
toll by adding up the many, many people (including hundreds of
police and firefighters involved in rescue work) who never
returned home.

Greg Sandow

Kevin,

According to several sites that track urban legends, the various
Nostradamus quatrains floating around about the attach are bogus.
Some are completely made up (apparently complete with dates of
authorship nearly a century after the big N died) or (as you guessed,
badly distorted versions of actual quatrains. For one such discussion

given the long and glorious history of bogus Nostradamus predictions,
I give the benefit of the doubt to those who argue he didn't say it.

All of those trying to take advantage of this tragedy, be they price
gougers, bomb threat hoaxers or Nostradamus friends propping up their
star, anger me to no end.

From: "Robinson, Larry" <lrobins@indiana.edu>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2001 11:07:39 -0500
Subject: RE: [UFORL] Oh shit...!

Centuries really start in years ending in ..01, and end in years ending
in ..00. This was known by everyone until the "new math" changed
how this is taught in schools.

The reason centuries and millennia start in years ending in ..01 is
that there was no year numbered 0. This is because the number 0
was not believed to be a number then. It could not be displayed in
the Roman numeral system, which was in use when the current
calendar was set up. Our Arabic numerals had not yet been invented.

The first century ran from year I to year C.
The second century ran from year CI to year CC.

All of the world's governments celebrated the beginning of the new
millennium in the wrong year.

List,
Today while walking back to the Uni carpark in Leicester I observed the following:

Four objects in a "Schwarm" formation.

They looked lensoid, ie tapered front and rear with thickened middles.

Each object was light grey to white on top and dark grey on the bottom.

The objects appeared to flash as they moved.

They moved in an undulating manner.

They were flying along against a grey overcast sky.

The were Mute Swans flying along the line of the canal.

Chris

explained by autokinesis.

>I wonder what other implications these events might have for

I can perceive how recent, tragic events could have a significant
effect.

Primarily, I would have thought that the lunatic 'government UFO
cover up' bandwagon will no longer even achieve the heights of
popular media ridicule. The present and predicted media climate
is not one which is likely to tolerate speculation about any
supposed nefarious USA government actions that have had a
devastating impact on America.

Least of all, claims about a 'UFO cover up' and 'alien abductions
cover up' that only a few - essentially those who make the
allegations [often proven as fallacious] - actually believe can
be evidenced as having some, 'only we know about the cover up'
reality.

There may be a number of other repercussions which we will see
develop as a consequence.


Is it perhaps a tangible conclusion that within the context of a
profound 'focused reality' which has been awakened, 'UFOs',
particularly when insinuated or proclaimed to be alien
spaceships, will be of significantly less 'fascination' in the
foreseeable future than they have been since Kenneth Arnold's
founding report of objects which the media completely
misconstrued and reported as 'flying saucers', in late June,
1947?

Obviously, there can never be any proof those formative 'flying
saucers' were 'real', 'flying saucers' never were, and the refuge
of believers has been that 'cover up' scenario.

Significantly, as also proven by the recently released UK
Ministry of Defence [MoD] 'Rendlesham' file, there is no
intrinsic UK 'UFO cover up', ironically verified in one of the
former 'secret' documents, when Nick Pope complains about such
allegations to a MoD colleague.

Hopefully, one day it will equally be proven there's no American
'UFO cover up' and that will equally put an end to the nonsense.

So, where does 'ufology' go from here?

Where do fundamental 'believers' go from here.

Different questions, which will no doubt have diverse outcomes
that should redefine 'ufology'.

Meantime, attacking the US goverment for its 'crimes against
humanity'... we can leave to Greer, and all of those, the many,
who have supported that accusation.

From: "Robinson, Larry" <lrobins@indiana.edu>
Date: Thu, 20 Sep 2001 09:25:50 -0500
Subject: RE: [UFORL] US UFO sightings during grounding

There are a few things that could explain the hum. Two of them
even explains why only some people hear it.

1. Power lines vibrating: When power lines are carrying heavy
currents, the lines themselves can give off a humming sound if they
happen to be acoustically resonant at power line frequencies. This
should occur at 30, 60, 120, or 180 Hz in the US and Canada, and
25, 50, 100, or 150 Hz elsewhere in the world.

The rapid increase in the use of discharge lighting has resulted in an
unexpected 180 or 150 Hz (depending on locality) 3rd harmonic
component to appear on power lines. Lines originally damped out at
60 or 50 Hz can make audible noise at 180 or 150 Hz. This effect
also can make noises by unbalancing 3-phase power systems. The
light fixtures themselves, and pole transformers can also make
audible noises at 120 and 360 Hz, or 100 and 300 Hz (depending
on locality), twice the frequencies on the lines.

This sound was probably always there, but not noticed until the lack
of traffic (everyone home watching the news) lowered the background
noise enough to make it audible.

Has anyone done a study to find out the frequency of the reported
hum? It should prove interesting, especially if the frequency is a
harmonic of 60 Hz in the US and Canada, and 50 Hz elsewhere.

2. Low frequency tinnitus: During a sonic boom, a loud thunderclap,
or some other loud low frequency sound, it is possible for cells in
the Organ of Corti to be temporarily or permanently damaged. Until
the brain learns to ignore the signals from these cells (or they heal),
it will report a ringing (or in the case of LF damage, humming) sound.

3. Miniscule noises: If the low frequency noise is atonal, it just
might be that the witness was in a location quiet enough to hear
noises coming from two sources:

- The Brownian motion of air molecules, bouncing off the eardrum.

- Blood cells moving through capillaries in the area of the ear.

These are the same effects that put "the ocean" in a shell held to
the ear. Cover your ears with your hands to hear these sounds.

Remember that the ear contains a compressor network in the
ossicles. This magnifies the sound level to the listener under very
quiet conditions.

From: Frits Westra <fwestra@hetnet.nl>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2001 13:37:51 +0200
Subject: [UFORL] Fwd = UFO reporting instructions now in FAA procedures

Hello all,

You may know that for many years the US Air Force has pilot instructions
for UFO reporting (CIRVIS instructions) in section B-39 of the DoD Flight
Information Handbook (FIH).

Since July 2001, the US Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) is for the
first time including a paragraph about UFO reports in its Aeronautical
Information Manual (AIM). The UFO reporting instructions are in Section 6,
par. 7-6-4, Safety, Accident, and Hazard Reports (full text appended
below):

 http://www.faa.gov/ATpubs/AIM/Chap7/aim0706.html

The identical text has also appeared in the FAA Air Traffic Control
procedures order (7110.65M), Section 9, par. 9-9-1, Unidentified Flying
Object (UFO) Reports:

 http://www.faa.gov/ATpubs/ATC/Chp9/atc0909.html

Kind regards,
Frits Westra -- fwestra@despammed.com
=====================================

   AIM 7-6-4. Unidentified Flying Object (UFO) Reports

   a. Persons wanting to report UFO activity should contact the
   National Institute for Discovery Sciences (NIDS) via the following
   methods:

   (702) 798-1700 Voice
   (702) 798-1970 Facsimile
   http://www.nidsci.org

   b. NIDS will ask a series of questions (verbal and/or via
   questionnaire) concerning the event.

   NOTE-
   NIDS is the single point of contact recognized by the FAA in regard
   to UFO information. They will maintain a national database on
   anomalous phenomena and periodically share that information with
   the FAA.

   c. If concern is expressed that life or property might be
   endangered, refer the individual to the local police department.

From: "James Easton" <voyager@ufoworld.co.uk>
Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2001 04:17:24 +0100
Subject: [UFORL] Rendlesham: Radiation Readings

This is a preamble to some detailed new information which is
emerging about the radiation readings recorded when Lt. Col. Halt
and others investigated reports the 'UFO was back'.

Effectively, Halt's assembled team of "specialists" then headed
out into Rendlesham forest to the supposed 'landing site', where
some ground indentations had subsequently been noticed following
Burroughs, Cabansag and Penniston's earlier 'encounter'.

Included in Halt's team was Sergeant Monroe Nevilles, the
Disaster Preparedness NCO, who brought with him a Geiger counter.
It's understood Nevilles used the standard AN/PDR-27 Geiger
counter - see:

http://www.torontosurplus.com/scientific/DATA650.JPG

Halt's microcassette recording of events contains several
references to the radiation readings and although it's long been
obvious these were of no significance, Nick Pope has cited how
Halt's memo to the Ministry of Defence [MoD] reported levels
which Pope was able to confirm as ten times higher than normal
background radiation.

Indeed, Pope claims these high levels are, "the most tangible
proof that something extraordinary happened there".

I'm confident it can now be definitively proven that the 'ten
times higher' levels documented in Halt's memo were in fact, ten
times higher than those readings actually were.


The most conspicuous clues from Halt's tape recording are:

HALT: That's the best deflection of the needle I've seen yet. OK,
can you give me an estimation. We're on the point five
scale...we're getting...I have trouble reading the scale...

[...]

HALT: Up to seven tenths? Or seven units, let's call it, on the
point five scale.
[END]


What was the "point five scale"?
On the AN/PDR-27, there were four ranges of sensitivity which
could be selected:

X1 - between 0-.5 milliroentgens
X10 - between 0-5 milliroentgens
X100 - between 0-50 milliroentgens
X1000 - between 0-500 milliroentgens

See for example:

http://www.execpc.com/~dcshop69/ppttxt.htm

As an informed source further explains:

"Radiation is frequently measured in units called milliroentgens.
A milliroentgen is 1/1000th of a roentgen. In turn, a roentgen by
definition is 'the unit of radiation exposure in the air.' Geiger
counters, radiac sets, and survey meters measure the radiation at
the rate of milliroentgens per hour (mR/h).

military personnel familiar with the AN/PDR-27 have told me the
numeric scale read from 0 to 0.5 in 0.010 intervals. (This unit
is no longer in military service). The beta/gamma detection
capability is controlled by an adjustment on the probe. The
AN/PDR-27 has four ranges of sensitivity: 0 to 0.5 mR/h, 0 to 5
mR/h, 0 to 50 mR/h, and 0 to 500 mR/h. The operator would select
the range by use of the multiplier switch on the AN/PDR-27 panel.
The multiplier switch has four positions for the four sensitivity
ranges. These four positions are labeled X1, X10, X100, and
X1000. Example of how this would work: say the operator has the
multiplier switch set to X1 and obtains a reading on the scale at
0.3. This would mean that radiation has been detected at the rate
of 0.3 mR/h. Now, the operator sets the multiplier switch to the
X10 position and obtains a reading at 0.3 on the numeric scale.
This would actually mean the radiation has been detected at 3.0
mR/h because we have multiplied the values on the scale by 10
times (X10). The intervals on the scale would also increase in
value ten times so on the X10 range they would jump from 0.01 to
0.1. The X100 setting would increase the value on the scale 100
times (0 to 50 mR/h range), and the X1000 setting would increase
it a thousand times (0 to 500 mR/h range). Keep in mind that as
you increase the multiplier settings; you lessen the detection
sensitivity. The most sensitive detection range is the X1 setting
(0 to 0.5 mR/h)".

Halt's memo claims:

"...the area was checked for radiation. Beta/gamma readings of
0.1 milliroentgens were recorded with peak readings in the three
depressions and near the center of the triangle formed by the
depressions. A nearby tree had moderate (0.5-0.7) readings on the
side of the tree toward the depressions".

On the 'point five scale', it's obviously impossible to obtain a
reading greater than 0.5 mR/h. This has been substantiated.

That could only have occurred if the AN/PDR-27 setting was 'X10 -
between 0-5 milliroentgens', or higher.

However, Halt confirms they were utilising, as we would expect,
the most sensitive setting.

Consequently, the 'minor clicks' and levels of 'up to seven
clicks' etc. which were being observed on the 'point five scale'
must have been between 0.05 and 0.07 mR/h.

This is precisely the scenario which Ian Ridpath's separate,
published research had concluded.

Typical background radiation.


As noted, there's a more detailed analysis which will be
published shortly. Meantime, it's at the very least now evidenced
why on the 'point five scale' you can't go beyond 'point five',
as Halt informed the MoD and which Nick Pope proclaims the "most
tangible proof" ET was there...


James Easton.

<HTML><FONT FACE=arial,helvetica><FONT SIZE=2>James,
<BR>The picture brings back memories.
<BR>
<BR>"This unit is no longer in military service"
<BR>
<BR>The Navy is still using it from the best of my knowledge (at least as of a year
and a half ago when I retired - there was no replacement).
<BR>
<BR>I do believe I told you some time ago that the number of clicks that were
audible was directly proportional to the amount of radiation being detected.
&nbsp;The values were somewhere in the range of a 200-300 counts per minute for
just 0.1 mr reading (maybe the makers could give you a better value but this is the
number I recall). &nbsp;The purpose of the headset and these count relations was not
for measuring purposes but to alert the operator of any significant counts when he was
doing his survey. &nbsp;In the tape we are hearing the operators talk about a couple
of clicks (per minute, per second, or just total clicks?), which means the radiation
level was very low (even lower than the value of 0.07 mr which is what I think they
really meant was the highest reading seen). &nbsp;The 0.07 mr value should have
given the operators something on the order of 2-3 clicks per second! &nbsp;I think if
the operators actually heard a few clicks a second they might have been alarme!
d, especially if they were not familiar with the equipment (Nevilles seems to lack
proficiency based on the tape). &nbsp;The reason for the 0.07 reading not conforming
to the number of clicks is probably due to inexperienced operators waving the unit
around. &nbsp;Not shown in the picture is a shoulder strap for keeping the unit steady
when carrying it about. &nbsp;These meter pointers were very sensitive to motion.
&nbsp;This is probably one of the reasons for the unit spiking up towards 0.07 mr/hr
(which is not too high for background values anyway). &nbsp;Additionally, if the
beta window was open (at the end of the large probe - I notice the picture angle only
shows the large probe, there is a smaller one piggyback on the opposite side of the
probe shown), there would be a higher reading on the 27 as well since it would have
been measuring both Beta (low energy emissions - Beta particles) and Gamma (high
energy emission - Gamma rays) radiation.
<BR>
<BR>Actually, I think Nevilles choice of the 27 was not a good one. It is best suited
for measuring radiation and he should have been concerned about contamination. This
would have required the use of an E-140N unit instead (assuming the AF was using
the same equipment we squids used). &nbsp;
<BR>
<BR>Keep up the good work. Anyone trying to present the radiation levels as
something unusual is way out in left field. &nbsp;
<BR>
<BR>Tim Printy</FONT>

>From: "James Easton" <voyager@ufoworld.co.uk>

>Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2001 04:17:24 +0100

>This is a preamble to some detailed new information which is
>emerging about the radiation readings recorded when Lt. Col. Halt
>and others investigated reports the 'UFO was back'.
>
>Effectively, Halt's assembled team of "specialists" then headed
>out into Rendlesham forest to the supposed 'landing site', where
>some ground indentations had subsequently been noticed following
>Burroughs, Cabansag and Penniston's earlier 'encounter'.
>
>Included in Halt's team was Sergeant Monroe Nevilles, the
>Disaster Preparedness NCO, who brought with him a Geiger counter.
>It's understood Nevilles used the standard AN/PDR-27 Geiger
>counter - see:
>
>http://www.torontosurplus.com/scientific/DATA650.JPG
>
>Halt's microcassette recording of events contains several
>references to the radiation readings and although it's long been
>obvious these were of no significance, Nick Pope has cited how
>Halt's memo to the Ministry of Defence [MoD] reported levels
>which Pope was able to confirm as ten times higher than normal
>background radiation.
>
>Indeed, Pope claims these high levels are, "the most tangible
>proof that something extraordinary happened there".
>
>I'm confident it can now be definitively proven that the 'ten
>times higher' levels documented in Halt's memo were in fact, ten
>times higher than those readings actually were.
>
>
>The most conspicuous clues from Halt's tape recording are:
>
>HALT: That's the best deflection of the needle I've seen yet. OK,
>can you give me an estimation. We're on the point five
>scale...we're getting...I have trouble reading the scale...
>
>[...]
>
>HALT: Up to seven tenths? Or seven units, let's call it, on the
>point five scale.
>[END]
>
>
>What was the "point five scale"?
>
>On the AN/PDR-27, there were four ranges of sensitivity which
>could be selected:
>
>X1 - between 0-.5 milliroentgens
>X10 - between 0-5 milliroentgens
>X100 - between 0-50 milliroentgens
>X1000 - between 0-500 milliroentgens
>
>See for example:
>
>http://www.execpc.com/~dcshop69/ppttxt.htm
>
>As an informed source further explains:
>
>"Radiation is frequently measured in units called milliroentgens.
>A milliroentgen is 1/1000th of a roentgen. In turn, a roentgen by
>definition is 'the unit of radiation exposure in the air.' Geiger
>counters, radiac sets, and survey meters measure the radiation at
>the rate of milliroentgens per hour (mR/h).
>
>military personnel familiar with the AN/PDR-27 have told me the
>numeric scale read from 0 to 0.5 in 0.010 intervals. (This unit
>is no longer in military service). The beta/gamma detection
>capability is controlled by an adjustment on the probe. The
>AN/PDR-27 has four ranges of sensitivity: 0 to 0.5 mR/h, 0 to 5
>mR/h, 0 to 50 mR/h, and 0 to 500 mR/h. The operator would select
>the range by use of the multiplier switch on the AN/PDR-27 panel.
>The multiplier switch has four positions for the four sensitivity
>ranges. These four positions are labeled X1, X10, X100, and
>X1000. Example of how this would work: say the operator has the
>multiplier switch set to X1 and obtains a reading on the scale at
>0.3. This would mean that radiation has been detected at the rate
>of 0.3 mR/h. Now, the operator sets the multiplier switch to the
>X10 position and obtains a reading at 0.3 on the numeric scale.
>This would actually mean the radiation has been detected at 3.0
>mR/h because we have multiplied the values on the scale by 10
>times (X10). The intervals on the scale would also increase in
>value ten times so on the X10 range they would jump from 0.01 to
>0.1. The X100 setting would increase the value on the scale 100
>times (0 to 50 mR/h range), and the X1000 setting would increase
>it a thousand times (0 to 500 mR/h range). Keep in mind that as
>you increase the multiplier settings; you lessen the detection
>sensitivity. The most sensitive detection range is the X1 setting
>(0 to 0.5 mR/h)".
>
>Halt's memo claims:
>
>"...the area was checked for radiation. Beta/gamma readings of
>0.1 milliroentgens were recorded with peak readings in the three
>depressions and near the center of the triangle formed by the
>depressions. A nearby tree had moderate (0.5-0.7) readings on the
>side of the tree toward the depressions".
>
>On the 'point five scale', it's obviously impossible to obtain a
>reading greater than 0.5 mR/h. This has been substantiated.
>
>That could only have occurred if the AN/PDR-27 setting was 'X10 -
>between 0-5 milliroentgens', or higher.
>
>However, Halt confirms they were utilising, as we would expect,
>the most sensitive setting.
>
>Consequently, the 'minor clicks' and levels of 'up to seven
>clicks' etc. which were being observed on the 'point five scale'
>must have been between 0.05 and 0.07 mR/h.
>
>This is precisely the scenario which Ian Ridpath's separate,
>published research had concluded.
>
>Typical background radiation.
>
>
>As noted, there's a more detailed analysis which will be
>published shortly. Meantime, it's at the very least now evidenced
>why on the 'point five scale' you can't go beyond 'point five',
>as Halt informed the MoD and which Nick Pope proclaims the "most
>tangible proof" ET was there...

>fatrob83 wrote:
>
>"what type of display did the meter use?(lcd or sliding/swinging needle).
>If the needle type any idea how many graduation marks it had?"
>
>
>The meter was an analog "swinging needle" type. The graduations were 50
>minor divisions and five major (every 10 minor divisions). The ranges were
>already noted by James by were in ranges of 5 (i.e. 0-0.5 mr, 0-5mr) so the
>operator could easily determine the reading without any difficulty. The 7
>minor divisions discussed made the readings 0.07 mr/hr.
>
>Tim Printy

Tim,

Yes, you did and all of the pieces concerning this particular
puzzle seem be falling into place.

>The purpose of the headset and these count relations was not for
>measuring purposes but to alert the operator of any significant
>counts when he was doing his survey.

That's helpful to know.

>I think if the operators actually heard a few clicks a second
>they might have been alarmed, especially if they were not
>familiar with the equipment (Nevilles seems to lack proficiency
>based on the tape).

Ian Ridpath informs that Major James McGaha researched this case
as a member of CSICOP when stationed on the base complex in 1986.
McGaha explained that Sergeant Nevilles was an equipment
custodian in Disaster Preparedness [DP] - that's why he had
access to the Geiger counter. DP were never officially requested
to investigate and held no record of the incident.

There's a related document which I have seen. Following a 1984
query from CNN, the public affairs office at Bentwaters confirmed
DP had no involvement.

>The reason for the 0.07 reading not conforming to the number of
>clicks is probably due to inexperienced operators waving the
>unit around. Not shown in the picture is a shoulder strap for
>keeping the unit steady when carrying it about. These meter
>pointers were very sensitive to motion.
That was the understanding, Ian Ridpath having been duly advised
by Giles Cowling from the UK's DERA Radiation Protection
Services. There's a detailed background to this within 'Resolving
Rendlesham' - see:

www.rendlesham.com

This, incidentally, is the new home for my online case material.


>Additionally, if the beta window was open...

I note Robert McLean has, amazingly, been able to answer your
astute question.

>Actually, I think Nevilles choice of the 27 was not a good one.
>It is best suited for measuring radiation and he should have
>been concerned about contamination. This would have required the
>use of an E-140N unit instead (assuming the AF was using the
>same equipment we squids used).

Can you please clarify what the difference was between these
units? Did the E-140N use the same four ranges, including a
'point five' scale?

I also understand that we could have expected DP personnel to be
equipped with a dosimeter. I believe this is pen-sized, attached
to external clothing and measures the amount of accumulated
radiation exposure in roentgens.

From: TPrinty@aol.com
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2001 18:52:18 EDT
Subject: Re: [UFORL] Rendlesham: Radiation Readings
boundary="part1_5f.1bb927c8.28ecf0a2_boundary"

<x-html>
<HTML><FONT FACE=arial,helvetica><FONT SIZE=2>James wrote:
<BR>
<BR>"Can you please clarify what the difference was between these
<BR>units? Did the E-140N use the same four ranges, including a
<BR>'point five' scale?"
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>The E-140N is a type of detector used to measure very low level Beta-gamma
contamination/radiation. &nbsp;I do recall the levels being on the order of 0-500, 0-
5000, 0-50000 Counts Per Minute (there may have been another range but I really
can't recall and even these values may be off). There is a thumbrule to convert CPM
to mR/hr. &nbsp;The key point being that 100 CPM above background relating to the
lowest detectable limit for radiation contamination (450 X10^-12 ci/100cm^2).
&nbsp;The difference between contamination and radiation is something akin to dog
droppings. &nbsp;The contamination is the droppings and the smell is the radiation.
&nbsp;A crude way of describing the difference but it used to work for the untrained
members of our crew. &nbsp;If they were looking for what was left by a UFO or even
an atomic device, the use of this type of detector would have been used (although for
a nuclear weapon they probably use an alpha detector as well - but that is a diff!
erent story all together).
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>"I also understand that we could have expected DP personnel to be
<BR>equipped with a dosimeter. I believe this is pen-sized, attached
<BR>to external clothing and measures the amount of accumulated
<BR>radiation exposure in roentgens."
<BR>
<BR>This is a pretty good description. &nbsp;Actually it usually is measured in rem
which is the equivalent damage for a given level of radiation. &nbsp;When discussing
gamma radation the roentgen and rem were the same values. &nbsp;There were
several types but the one I remember using was the one with the 0-200mr (or maybe it
was 0-50 see what old age does to you and it was only a year and a half ago that I
retired) scale (I think it was called the IM-9). &nbsp;These were very sensitive and if
dropped or banged the right way would result in an off-scale or errant reading. It
seems the Navy and AF did use some of the same equipment but I am not sure if that
was always the case.
<BR>
<BR>Tim Printy</FONT>
<br>

Subject: Re: [UFORL] Rendlesham: Radiation Readings

Regarding:

>From: <TPrinty@aol.com>
>To: <UFORL@yahoogroups.com>
>Subject: Re: [UFORL] Rendlesham: Radiation Readings
>Date: 04 October 2001 01:24

Tim wrote:

>The E-140N is a type of detector used to measure very low level
>Beta-gamma contamination/radiation.

Tim,

Thanks for your explanations and comments.

As I initially stated, "It's understood Nevilles used the
standard AN/PDR-27 Geiger counter".

I've been tracing back the origin of that understanding and the
AN/PDR-27 seems to have first been cited on the 1994 UK 'Strange
But True?' TV series - when they had a studio debate about
'UFOs'. Naturally, 'Rendlesham' featured, especially as 'Strange
But True?' had previously dedicated an entire program to it.

One of the 'skeptics' panel was Professor Frank Close. Col. Halt
was an invited guest and when the topic of those radiation
readings came up, Close produced an AN/PDR-27 - as the standard
USAF Geiger counter in use during December 1980 - demonstrating
to Halt how the readings were minuscule. It wasn't evident at
that time, how insignificant the levels truly were.

So far as I'm aware, Sgt. Nevilles never spoke about his
involvement and it's therefore presumed the AN/PDR-27 was almost
certainly what was used. All facts appear to agree with that.
Certainly, Halt didn't express any objections when he saw the
AN/PDR-27.

Would you agree it's now clear there are no other candidates and
it must have been that model, or comparative, which Nevilles
used?

I still have that 1994 program on tape, somewhere, and I'll look
it out over the weekend.
Incidentally, during September 1991, 'Unsolved Mysteries' also
broadcast a 'Rendlesham' documentary. If anybody has a copy of
this, or known where I might obtain one, would you please let me
know.


James Easton.

From: joel carpenter <ufx1947@home.com>Date: 04 October 2001 22:08

>Does anyone have any background information on this short video of a small

Hi,

Discovery asked you - too - did they?

It 'was; filmed during a test flight in the early 70s I think when
promo shots were being taken.

I understand - from talking to one of the camera crew years ago - that it is
believed to have probably been a small
piece of grit caught in the camera lens that reflected the sun abd moves
with the lens and so appears
to move across the aircraft in the process.

But there are many similar cases to this one. In my book 'Something in the
Air' (l998) (UFO Danger in the Air - US title) I cover many examples or
such mid air encounters that are nearly identical - which are not, of
course, so explained.

I have twice been personally involved (both are in the book). In one case in
the 60s I saw an object tail an aircraft them zip away - much as in the
Concorde case. This incident was a toy balloon caught in the slipstream of
the plane and tossed free as it banked. I saw it happen. Some of the cases I
report in the book are explainable in this way - but others obviously are
not.

The second was a terrifying flight in January l995 across the gale tossed
Irish Sea. We had to be diverted and whilst I saw nothing a witness called
Jodrell Bank (who pass cases onto me for follow up) and reported seeing a
small white blob pace the aircraft then zip away - again like so many other
cases. The plane she was watching as she walked her dog was apparently the
one I was sat on then approaching Leeds/Bradford airport.

So I have an open mind on this increasingly common problem!
Best wishes,

Jenny Randles

From: "James Easton" <voyager@ufoworld.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2001 04:01:06 +0100
Subject: Re: [UFORL] Rendlesham: Radiation Readings

Thanks to Tim Printy's clarifications, someone has kindly
provided the scan of a comparative dial. It's been uploaded to
the Rendlesham web site, at:

http://www.rendlesham.com/meter.gif

I'm advised the dial is from an American Civil Defense CDV700
Geiger counter, similar to the AN/PDR-27, except that the
graduations were marked in 0.020 increments.

The scan was edited to add 0.010 graduations and perhaps Tim can
confirm this now matches the AN/PDR-27 dial.

Some further comments received:

"It is important to note that the numbers actually printed on the
scale never change. The scale will always read 0 to 0.50 mR/h. It
is imperative for the operator to mathematically change the
number values when changing the range settings, i.e., if the
operator has the range setting set to X10 and the needle points
to 0.30 on the scale the operator must remember to multiply that
number ten times to get the proper reading of 3.0. It sounds as
if there may have been some confusion with this when obtaining
the readings from Rendlesham.

The AN/PDR-27 Radiac set was equipped with two probes. The larger
probe was utilized to obtain readings in the lower (more
sensitive) range, 0 to 0.50 mR/h & 0 to 5 mR/h, while the smaller
probe obtained readings in the higher (less sensitive) range, 0
to 50 mR/h & 0 to 500 mR/h. The larger probe was equipped with
the beta shield. It is safe to surmise that the larger probe were
utilized to obtain the readings in Rendlesham.

This information relative to the measurements on the scale would
now seem to corroborate the fact that the readings obtained in
the forest utilizing the 'point five scale' are, in my opinion,
not of any consequence. This was the most sensitive range setting
and this is also the setting that is highly susceptible to
picking up normal background radiation. If there had been any
significant radiation present, I'm sure it would have been
detected in one of the less sensitive ranges".
[END]


To reiterate, these are the relevant readings confirmed on the
'Halt tape':
HALT: You want to read that on the scale?

VOICE: Yes, sir. We're now on the five-tenths scale, and we're
reading about third, fourth [mark?] over...

[...]

HALT: That's the best deflection of the needle I've seen yet. OK,
can you give me an estimation. We're on the point five
scale...we're getting...I have trouble reading the scale...

VOICE: At approximately 0125 hours...

VOICE: We're getting rad at half a millirem.

[...]

VOICE: ...up towards seven...just jumped up towards seven tenths.

HALT: Seven tenths? Right there in the center?

[...]

HALT: Up to seven tenths? Or seven units, let's call it, on the
point five scale.
[END]


It seems we can now definitively evidence that the levels being
obtained peaked at 0.07 mR/h and not the 0.7 mR/h reported in
Halt's memo to the Ministry of Defence.


Halt has expressed his belief that the levels detected were not
dangerous, although they were above normal background readings.
He elaborated during the May 13, 1997 'Project: watchfire' on-
line interview and Q&A session with Salley Rayl. Halt is
describing how events unfolded that second night:

RAYL: And what was the general situation out there?

HALT: There were probably 25 to 30 security policemen there. They
were kind of stirring about trying to get the light-alls going
and all excited and pointing into the forest and the Lieutenant
that had taken us or picked me up at the Officers' Mess handed me
a Starlight scope and said, "Look into the forest," and pointed
to an area and [I] looked in and saw a glowing area. Nothing one
could discern exactly, but just a glowing area... And, of course
RAYL: Had you ever seen anything like that before?

HALT: No. I'd used the Starlight scope quite a few times, and it
was obviously some kind of energy or some type of light. I don't
really know what it was to this day.

RAYL: What did you decide to do then?

HALT: Well, we decided to go into the forest and investigate and
they pointed out to me that they'd been into the supposed landing
site where something had landed or had been stationed on the
ground two nights before and we went into the forest and the
approximate area where we'd seen the glow, they found and pointed
out to me three indentations in the floor of the forest.

RAYL: And you did what next?

HALT: Well, I had an individual from Disaster Preparedness with
me with what you would call a Geiger counter and he started
taking readings and we were looking at indentations. I'd taken
along a small pocket micro-cassette recorder because it was kind
of a cold winter night and I thought I might need to take some
notes. Because the intent was really to put this whole thing to
bed. And while we were milling about and identifying spots and
taking readings, we noticed on the trees some rub marks on the
trees facing the indentations in the ground and the Geiger
counter indicated it was a little warmer there. Nothing of any
danger, really, in my opinion, but certainly something above
background radiation. But, the other side of the tree was much
colder and while we were doing that, suddenly the Lieutenant
pointed off to the, toward, the farmer's field, said, "Look over
here." And he saw something.
[END OF EXTRACT]

As Robert has mentioned, the Lieutenant was Bruce England [Duty
Flight Lieutenant].


It's primarily Nick Pope who has cited 'radiation levels' to be
foremost evidence of an alien spacecraft landing, as Pope related
to 'UFO Magazine' [UK] in a formative interview on 5 May 1996:

Nick Pope: I can reveal that because there was so much interest
in this case, even during my time at Sec(AS)2a, I made some
efforts to have a retrospective look into it, but it was very
difficult. One thing I did do was to take the raw data from the
Halt memorandum and gave it to the Defence Radiological Service
and I said, what do you make of these readings? [radiation
information contained within the Halt letter]. It had of course
occurred to me that there was background radiation anyway and
suppose Halt had simply taken readings of this? The quote I got
back from the board was, "what the hell happened there?" I said,
what do you mean. They told me that the radiation readings were
ten times what they should have been in that area. I then faxed
them the full report, I think that day there were a few new
converts!

UFO Magazine: Was there a cover-up?

Nick Pope: No. Not in the MoD - I think the MoD's response was
just ineffective.

UFO Magazine: That's a very big statement?

Nick Pope: Yes, but if something of that magnitude was reported
and simply placed on file, then what else can you say?
[END OF EXTRACT]


Obviously, we now know, as does Pope, that the MoD did in fact
investigate Halt's claims.


On 23rd May 1998, in an Internet Relay Chat [IRC] hosted by the
United Kingdom UFO Network, Pope was asked:

"What in your opinion is the most credible of all UK UFO related
cases and why?"

He replied: "I'd say it was the Rendlesham Forest incident, and
it's the radiation readings that clinched it for me. I checked
them out with the Defence Radiological Protection Service, who
told me they were ten times normal for the area".

Another participant queried: "Have you reconsidered your position
about the radiation levels found at Bentwaters? As Frank Close
pointed out on the telly, most rocks are considerably higher than
the background levels. These levels *would* be significant
background levels, but they weren't".

Pope responded: "Frank Close was entirely correct when he said
the radiation levels were harmless. Halt and his team were in no
danger. But the levels were ten times what they should have been
in that area, and they peaked at the landing site. This was
confirmed to me by government scientists. It is an official
assessment, and is not in dispute".


Bottom line, as Ian Ridpath noted: "In his book 'Open Skies,
Closed Minds', Nick Pope described the radiation readings as 'the
most tangible proof that something extraordinary happened there'.
Hence it is essential that the readings are shown to be beyond
reproach".


I trust they are now shown, as Ian had already surmised, to be
ten times less than Halt's understanding, which Pope and others
put so much pivotal faith in.

If, "the most tangible proof that something extraordinary
happened there" turns out to be evidence of blundering human
error, it can only further set in a factual context, Britain's
'Roswell'.


James Easton.
E-mail: voyager@ufoworld.co.uk
www.ufoworld.co.uk
